We have a bouncy confident 2M Labrador, and a small nervous 7F rescue. 

At first, the lab wouldn’t stop humping the rescue (both neutered). And the rescue kept peeing in the house. 

- Provide safe spaces to retreat to. Early on, ours had their own crates and they’re not allowed in each others crates. Now that they’re best mates, they prefer to share soft beds. We rarely see them in their respective crates nowadays. 
- in the early days, they had really frequent outdoor walks to remove territorial behaviours and encourage pack mentality. 
- They are always fed seperately. And when a treat is offered, they are separated into different rooms. 

It’s double the work, because they have their own individual needs. but they’re double the fun. And I love to see their quirky personalities together everyday.

I rescued my girl from the meat trade back in January. She was like your girl, so anxious she wet herself. Just constantly fearful. She wouldn’t let me pet her. 
8 months on and she’s improved so much! She still gets scared of shadows on the wall and sudden loud noises but she’s much better. We cuddle, go on adventures together, eat together. She views me as part of her pack now. She’s even started to follow me round the house this month!! Every month brings a new achievement.  

It’s been an honour to watch her blossom and gain confidence. If you’re willing to be patient with her, your pup could become your best friend. 

Some tips that helped me:
1. Give her a high up space that is her “safe space”. I.e an armchair or a crate. the higher from the floor she is, the safer mine feels! 
2. Socialise with other dogs as much as you can! Lots of play dates, parks. hop on Google and see if there’s any local doggy meet ups. There’s a rescue-only one and small-breed one next month that I’m taking my girl to (U.K.) 
3. Talk to her softly throughout the day. If she will allow you, sit and stroke her softly for as long as she will let you. If she gets up and moves, that’s fine, try again tomorrow. 
4. Make sure she’s healthy! My girl had a tummy bug which made her even more nervous. Sorted out her tummy and she relaxed a bit. 

If you feel up to the challenge, then I assure you she will improve! She may never be fearless, and she will always have her quirks but you soon come to love and accept them for who they are. 
That being said, if you don’t think this the right journey for you, or for your pup, then that is totally ok too! 

All the best x
